gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-parkinsans: Neon tubes, spaced out letter by letter: that's Neuropolitical, glowing and geometric up top. Parkinsans follows in one steady stroke, its lowercase rising close to the capitals and staying crisp even when small.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-pathway-ext: Contemporary through and through, Neuropolitical sets its neon-tube letters apart one by one, while Pathway Extreme keeps a big x-height with stubby ascenders beneath. Rounded openings stay clear.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-preahvihear: Preahvihear gapes wide in every letter mouth, like a pried oyster shell, with a lofty x-height holding up each line. Beneath Neuropolitical's glowing, spaced-out display letters, it reads easily.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-pt-sans-cap: PT Sans Caption brings big-bodied lowercase with inviting, unclosed bowls beneath the glowing, spaced-out neon letters of Neuropolitical. Shrink that heading and its tube-like glow would fade.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-puritan: Puritan reads in rounded forms that stay clearly open to the side, with oversized e and a counters. Neuropolitical's neon-tube heading, spaced out letter by letter, makes the starkest contrast to it.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-questrial: Neuropolitical pulls its words apart letter by letter, each neon-tube glyph glowing with a single line thickness. Questrial then carries the text in a tall, flat, stencil-cut band, steady and easy going.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-radio-canad: Glowing neon letters, spaced apart one at a time: Neuropolitical looks like a sign humming in the dark. Radio Canada's tall, full lowercase and open curve endings keep the text steady beneath it.

Contemporary and geometric, Neuropolitical lights its spaced-out letters like neon tubes with one line thickness throughout. Radio Canada Big carries a long stretch smoothly, its monoline strokes and tall x-height staying clear.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-readex-pro: Readex Pro reads with broad gaps at its terminals and a tiny gap between lowercase and caps, unvarying from word to word. And Neuropolitical's glowing, spaced-out neon letters are the opposite: all display flash.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-ruda: Ruda reads comfortably, with a sizable x-height, wire-thin monoline strokes and wide-mouthed rounds in the lowercase. Neuropolitical earns its keep big and short, its neon-tube letters spaced apart.
